trigger: Office move and Microsoft 365 migration before busy season

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Ben Wallace, thanks for taking the call. I have Elm & Ledger Accounting as a fifty-two person practice in Geelong, and you're one of the directors, correct?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Correct. We're moving offices at the end of September, and it has forced a decision about IT. We also want to finish a Microsoft 365 migration before the next busy season.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What is driving the Microsoft 365 migration now rather than after the move?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: We're halfway between old file shares and SharePoint. Staff are confused, and our current provider keeps telling us to wait. The office move feels like the clean moment to stop dragging both systems around.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: How does that confusion show up for accountants and admin during client work?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: People duplicate files, Xero reports end up in the wrong folder, and managers ask admin to find versions during client calls. Nobody is malicious; it's just messy and wastes time.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Who needs to be involved in approving the plan?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Me, another director, and our office manager. I can approve the managed service if the migration risk is clearly controlled. The office manager knows the staff pain better than anyone.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What are the non-negotiables for the office move weekend?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Internet live before Monday, printers mapped, Teams phones working, Xero and the tax software accessible, and no mystery about where client files live. We've no appetite for heroics on Monday morning.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Where do security and cyber insurance sit on your list?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Increasingly high. The insurer asked about MFA, backups and admin rights. Accounting firms are an obvious target, and clients assume we've our house in order.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: For Elm & Ledger Accounting, Harbourline would likely recommend managed services at $130 per seat per month, plus a fixed office move and Microsoft 365 migration project.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: We cannot have a messy migration in the middle of tax planning work. If staff lose client files or Xero access, the partners will never forgive the change.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Agreed. The migration should be staged, tested with a pilot group and frozen around key lodgement dates. I will send the office move checklist and migration proposal by Wednesday so you can see the exact order.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: That would help. I also want someone to look at old Xero access. We've former contractors who may still have permissions.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I will include the Xero access review and the busy-season support plan. The onboarding project will document users, permissions, backups and the move-weekend run sheet.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: That sounds like the right level. Price is within range if the migration is fixed fee and we can hold you to the run sheet.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Can we do a site walk-through Wednesday 9 September at 10am with you and the office manager, then finalise the proposal that afternoon?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Yes, Wednesday 9 September at 10am works. Come to the current office and we can show you the comms room and the file structure.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: For the walk-through, I will want to see the comms cupboard, sample client folders, current permissions and the move timetable. That keeps the quote tied to reality.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Good. We've had people quote from a phone call before, and then every exception became a variation. I'd rather expose the messy parts upfront.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: We will also mark anything that shouldn't move during the office weekend. Some legacy data may be better archived cleanly than dragged into the new structure.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: That will be a useful discipline. Accountants tend to keep everything forever, and then complain that search is terrible.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: The support plan will include extra cover for the first Monday and a named escalation path, so your office manager isn't standing between staff and the provider.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: She will appreciate that. She is excellent, but she has become the unofficial queue for every technical complaint.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I will also ask about your lodgement calendar during the walk-through. It's easy for IT people to plan around their own availability and accidentally land work during your worst possible week.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Please do. Our quiet-looking weeks can still have partner reviews, payroll and client deadlines packed inside them.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: For the proposal, I will make the assumptions visible: number of seats, current file volume, printer count, Xero users and which work happens after hours.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Good. Visible assumptions make it easier for the directors to approve, because they can see what would change the number.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Excellent. I will send the invite, checklist and proposal outline before then.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Ben Wallace
turns.text: Thanks Sam. If the walk-through checks out, we're ready to move quickly.
